name: 23441-imageprefill-9b-2gpu
hardware: 2x H100 80GB HBM3 on one a3 node, --gres=gpu:2.
architecture: Glm4vForConditionalGeneration (model_type glm4v), bf16, 10.3B params in four safetensors shards, 20.6 GB on the hub, ungated.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=128, bounded at 640 requests, 20% warmup, 10% cooldown (inert at a request bound), safety_seconds 2700 as a cap rather than an expectation.
workload: guidellm synthetic, two data specs merged: one unique 1920x1080 JPEG per request (q85, content gradient, seed 42) plus 64 fixed prompt tokens, answered in exactly 1000 output tokens.
purpose: A visual reasoning assistant describing one full-HD photo per request with long answers, 128 concurrent users, two GPUs.
launch:
model: zai-org/GLM-4.1V-9B-Thinking
tensor-parallel-size: 2
max-model-len: 16384
max-num-seqs: 128
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.9
dtype: bfloat16

# Also sizes max_num_encoder_input_tokens, so it must stay >= one image's encoder input
# (2691 tokens at 1080p). Written out because the default depends on how the engine is built.
max-num-batched-tokens: 8192

limit-mm-per-prompt: {"image": 1}

# Image preprocessing is paid on the client's single event loop, once per request, and at 1080p
# it is the slowest thing there. Both keys below only make that admission path cheaper; neither
# touches the model, the parallelism, the patch grid, the prompt or the decode length.
#
# `use_fast` selects transformers' torch-based Glm4vImageProcessorFast over the numpy/PIL one.
# GLM-4.1V is the only VL model in this engine whose ProcessingInfo does NOT ask for it (compare
# qwen2_vl.py, qwen2_5_vl.py, ernie45_vl.py, which all pass use_fast=True). Measured through
# vLLM's own MULTIMODAL_REGISTRY on this checkpoint, one 1920x1080 JPEG costs 0.282 s of CPU on
# the default path and 0.179 s on the fast one, for a byte-identical result: image_grid_thw
# [1, 78, 138], 10764 patches, 2691 image ids, 2700 prompt ids either way.
mm-processor-kwargs: {"use_fast": true}

# Every request in this workload carries a byte-distinct image (the synthetic generator advances
# its RNG per row), so the 4 GiB multimodal processor cache has a structural 0% hit rate. All it
# can do is cost a ~26 ms hash of the image plus a ~50 MB store-and-evict on every request.
mm-processor-cache-gb: 0
